get-product-availability.description:
Returns products available for a specific date. This includes capacity and session time information where supported.

> Availability depends on a number of factors:
> * **Dates** defined on the product, **times** defined in **schedules**, and **exclusion periods**
> * **Sale periods**, including **cut-off settings**
> * Capacity, which may be fixed/unlimited **quantity** or depend on **resource** settings
> * What the **product type** is, such as stock, session or party package
> * ...And other settings like `Hide from online sales`
> For more information on availability, please see our [**help centre**](https://mysupport.roller.software/hc/en-us/articles/6442667452431-Why-is-a-standard-pass-not-available-in-my-online-checkout).

get-product-availability-calendar.description:
Returns the availability status for each day in a given month for a single product. Designed for use in date picker and calendar UIs in third-party checkouts, allowing guests to see at a glance which dates have availability before selecting a specific date.

Once the guest has selected a date, call [**Get product availability**](#/paths/~1product-availability/get) to retrieve session-level detail and capacity for that date.

> Response data is cached for 1 minute and is invalidated when a new booking is created.

availability.description:
The availability status for this date:

- `available` — The product has capacity available
- `filling` — The product has limited capacity remaining
- `soldOut` — No capacity remaining on this date
- `notAvailable` — The product is not offered on this date (e.g. outside its schedule or in an exclusion period)
- `onlineSalesClosed` — The product exists but online sales are closed for this date (e.g. outside its sale period or past cut-off)

get-product-detail.description:
Returns product information for a venue.
> Changes in this data are not expected to change frequently. As such data must be cached and this endpoint used sparingly.
> Detail includes when the product is offered, but calls should be made to [**get product availability**](#/paths/~1product-availability/get) to determine if there's capacity on a given day.

get-price-rules.description:
Returns the active time-based price rules configured for the venue. Each rule describes the tiers a product can be priced at and when each tier applies, as recurring days of the week with optional times of day, and override date ranges.

The price each ticket type charges for a tier is not returned here. It is returned as `priceRule.timeTiers` on each ticket type by [**Get product detail**](#/paths/~1products/get). Join the two on `priceRuleId`, then match tiers on `tierId`. If a tier has no entry in `timeTiers`, the ticket type's base `price` applies.

Every other type of price rule (`quantity`, `earlyBird` and `capacity`) is described in full by **Get product detail** and is not returned here. See [**Price rules**](https://docs.roller.app/docs/api/price-rules) for how each type is applied.
> Changes in this data are not expected to be frequent. As such data must be cached and this endpoint used sparingly.

priceRuleId.description: Unique ID of the price rule. Matches `priceRuleId` on the product and on each ticket type's `priceRule` returned by **Get product detail**.

> Redeem tickets in ROLLER

* There is a maximum of 10 ticket redemptions per call
* Redeemed Ticket IDs must be unique per call
* Only the following products are supported for redemption via API:
  * Standard Passes
  * Session Passes
  * Recurring Sessions
  * Memberships (the booking item, not the membership discount)

redemptionDate.description: Optionally provide the redemption datetime in UTC. If not present, the datetime of the API call will be used

redemptionDevice.description: The name of the device where the ticket is being redeemed. Includes redemption devices, POS, MCI and SSK devices.

409.description:
Invalid redemption. 

Possible error messages:
* Ticket does not exist
* Booking Cancelled
* Ticket is not valid for this date
* Ticket IDs must be unique per request
* Ticket usage exhausted
* Product type not accepted
* Membership Invalid
* Ticket redemption usage exhausted
* Redemption device not found
* Duplicate custom ticket IDs found
* Custom ticket ID not found

If using **Redemption device** setting `Validate session times`:
* Ticket cannot be redeemed before the session start time
* Ticket cannot be redeemed after the session end time

create-gift-cards.description:
Create one or more gift cards for a single gift card product. Each entry in `giftCards` creates one card, and all cards are created against a single booking owned by `bookingOwner`.

Gift card numbers are returned in `giftCardNumbers`, in the same order as the request — a caller-supplied `giftCardNumber` is echoed back, otherwise a generated number is returned. Cards are activated asynchronously shortly after creation.

* `externalId` is unique per venue and acts as an idempotency key. Reusing one returns a `409`.
* `value` is required for open-value gift card products, and rejected for fixed-value products.
* A `recipient` must include both `name` and `email`, or neither.
* When `sendGiftCardEmails` is `true`, every card must have a recipient `name` and `email`.
* `deliveryDateTime` must be in the future (UTC).

externalId.description: External reference for this request. Unique per venue, and acts as an idempotency key.

productId.description: The ID of the gift card product to create cards from. Must be a gift card product in the venue.

bookingOwner.description: The primary contact for the booking the gift cards are created against.

email.description: Receives the booking confirmation when `sendConfirmations` is `true`.

giftCards.description: The gift cards to create. Each entry produces one card.

giftCardNumber.description: Optional custom gift card number. Must be unique within the request and the venue. Omit to have a number generated.

value.description: The value to load on the card. Required for open-value products, rejected for fixed-value products. Must be greater than zero.

recipient.description: The recipient the card is addressed to. Omit or set to null for an unassigned card.

message.description: Optional personal message shown on the card and in the recipient email.
message.example: Happy birthday! Enjoy a day out on us.

deliveryDateTime.description: Optional scheduled send time in UTC. Must be in the future, and requires a recipient `name` and `email`.

sendConfirmations.description: When `true`, sends the booking confirmation to the booking owner after creation.

sendGiftCardEmails.description: When `true`, sends each card's recipient their gift card email. Every card must then have a recipient `name` and `email`.

giftCardNumbers.description: The created gift card numbers, in the same order as the gift cards in the request. Caller-supplied numbers are echoed back; otherwise the generated number is returned.

400.description: Bad Request - The request body failed validation (eg: a required field is missing, an email is invalid, or a length limit is exceeded).

409.description: Conflict - A business rule was violated (eg: the externalId already exists, the product is not a gift card, or a gift card number is not unique).

get-gift-card-balance.description:
Get the current balance and details of a gift card by its number.

The gift card number is sent in the request body because gift card numbers may contain characters that are unsafe in a URL.

balance.description: The current balance of the gift card.

initialValue.description: The initial value of the gift card when it was issued. May be null, as this is not always available for external gift cards.

expiryDate.description: The date the gift card expires. If null, the gift card does not expire.

409.description: Conflict - The gift card could not be found, or the request was invalid (eg: gift card number is required).

bulk-data-export-request.description: Submit a bulk data export request. Once processed, a webhook of type `bulkExport` will be sent to subscribed endpoints containing presigned URL(s) to download the exported data.

exportType.description: The type of data to export.

startDate.description: The start date (inclusive) you need the data for. Format: `yyyy-MM-dd`

endDate.description:
The end date (exclusive) you need data for in ISO8601 date format (`yyyy-MM-dd`)

Note: Must be at least 1 day after `startDate`

Note: The end date is exclusive, so if you want data for all of July 2025:
- `startDate`: `2025-07-01`
- `endDate`: `2025-08-01`

params.name: TimeZone-Designators
params.description: Optional. By default all dates and times in the export files will be in UTC unless this header value is specified as `offset`, after which the venue timezone will be used instead. Note: This does not affect the date range parameters `startDate` or `endDate` which are always in the venue timezone.
